summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. Alphabet gets an explicit call today: neutral and low, because a deep fall alone has given no reason to expect a rebound. Nothing here is expected to beat the index; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: Big names jumped on the latest day, and Alphabet bounced a little after a long fall. A runner who fell is not sure to get up and win, and picking runners did no better than luck before. So the brain only watches with pretend money, and the family's real money keeps going into the whole-market basket every week.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. Nothing to do today; next week's buy of the whole-market fund comes on its usual day. Money we may need soon stays safe. We already own a small piece of Alphabet through that fund, and each weekly buy adds a little more at today's lower price, without us having to guess.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. The weekly bet game stands at two weeks won and one lost, and this week's bet is behind so far.

Third, a lesson. Alphabet has fallen far from its high while its filings still show a growing business. That is exactly when buying feels clever. But a fall alone tells us nothing about what comes next; sometimes a cheap thing gets cheaper. Our house rule is never to buy only because something fell a lot, and Berkshire, which disclosed it last year, is behind on it too.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain

bets.why: This week's bet was already placed and is repeated unchanged: names above their trend passing every setup check, against names below their trend whose checklist leaned down. No rule like this has beaten luck, so it is a learning bet only.

pick.thesis: An explicit first call on Alphabet after a deep fall. It sits far below its high for the year and below its fifty-day average, trails the benchmark on every window, and the chart checklist leans down; it bounced on the latest day. Its filing shows strong growth and margins but thin free cash flow. The house rule says never to buy only because a stock fell a lot, and no tested rule shows that deep falls on this list bounce back. Berkshire's disclosed book holds it bullishly but is behind; that record is the firm's, too thin to count.
